messages:
alex: Heads-up — we're prepping a Private deployment for ACME corp next week. Security asks landed: strict egress controls, KMS in their HSM, RBAC separation for platform vs customer ops, and 365-day immutable audit retention. Can we do a quick run-through of gaps?
sara: tl;dr: yes, but a few things to verify. what do they mean by 'KMS in their HSM' — cross-account HSM, or on-prem HSM directly attached to their VPC?
mike: They want a customer-managed HSM (on-prem appliance) with an envelope encryption flow. So runtime nodes call a local KMS endpoint, not AWS KMS. We need to confirm our gateway supports that.
jamie: note: our private agent has a KMS plugin that supports VENDOR-HSM endpoints over mTLS, but we only tested with SoftHSM and AWS CloudHSM. We should validate cert pinning + mutual TLS.
sec-bot: checklist suggestion: 1) egress allowlist (S3 endpoints, metrics, KMS) 2) deny-all-by-default network policy 3) KMS mTLS validation 4) audit pipeline with immutability 5) RBAC split: control-plane-admin vs infra-ops 6) documented key-rotation playbook.
alex: good. for egress: ACME requires no direct internet egress from inference nodes except to their internal artifact registry and their KMS. How do we enforce that in our helm chart / k8s manifests?
sara: use a combination of CNI network policy + iptables at kube-proxy? Better: install Calico with egress policies and use host-level nftables rules as last line of defense. Example NP snippet: ```yaml
apiVersion: projectcalico.org/v3
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-kms-and-registry
spec:
  selector: app == 'redwood-runtime'
  egress:
    - action: Allow
      destination:
        nets: ["10.10.0.0/16", "10.20.0.0/24"] # ACME KMS + registry
    - action: Deny
  order: 100
```
mike: small correction: Calico uses egress rules plus `action: Allow` then fallback is default deny if we set `types: ["Egress"]` and `selector`. We'll add a hostEndpoint rule to block undesired host-level egress too.
jamie: KMS integration notes: need to support OCSP + CRL checks for client certs, and map HSM identity to a Kubernetes ServiceAccount using SPIFFE or cert SAN mapping. Otherwise we can't audit which node used which key.
alex: on RBAC — ACME wants separation: their SREs must be able to restart pods and read logs but never access customer data or KMS decrypt. Our product currently has a `private-admin` role with broad perms. Proposal: add `private-runtime-ops` role limited to Pod/Node operations and `private-key-ops` only for key material rotation APIs (no data plane decrypt). Thoughts?
sara: sounds right. Implement via kube RBAC + our control plane ABAC to ban key-ops from console UI. Also add ephemeral `sudo` flow for key rotation that requires 2-person approval logged in audit.
sec-bot: recommend: enforce MFA + SSO for any role with key-ops. Record the approval in audit log entry with `approval_id` and attach to key-rotation event.
ops: for audit logging retention: ACME wants 365 days immutable. We can push signed audit bundles to their S3-compatible object store with object lock enabled (WORM). We should hash + sign each bundle and include manifest. Pipeline: `auditd -> fluent-bit -> gzip -> sign -> upload (object-lock)`.
mike: caveat: object-lock depends on provider. For true immutability with legal hold, we need customer-managed storage that supports retention overrides = false. We'll include TTL policy config and a fallback to storing signed manifest in their HSM.
jamie: vulnerability triage: if we discover a runtime CVE that requires node-level patching, plan is: 1) cordon node 2) spin new node with patched image 3) live-migrate KV caches 4) rotate KMS grants for the node identity 5) decommission old node and revoke any certs. Documented in incident runbook.
alex: and incident response for possible key compromise? quick checklist please.
sara: short checklist: 1) revoke key grants (HSM ACLs) 2) rotate master key (create new envelope key) 3) force re-encrypt of cached KV and persisted models 4) revoke node certs + rotate mTLS creds 5) run forensic audit on access logs and push to ACME sec team 6) failover to hosted cluster if customer allows.
jamie: addendum: ensure we have a 'dead-man's key' in customer HSM for emergency unwrap if key rotation fails; store emergency unwrap policy in sealed vault requiring 3-person access.
ops: rollout plan: night window with canary of 5% nodes in ACME dev VPC, run connectivity + KMS operations smoke tests: `kms:Encrypt`, `kms:Decrypt`, sign/verify. deploy-bot will create canary and report back.
sec-bot: automation: add runtime self-test that does a periodic `kms:describe` and `kms:sign` with latencies logged to console — alert if failures > 1% over 5m.
alex: ok next steps: jamie and mike to validate mTLS handshake against ACME HSM next Tues, sara to draft RBAC roles and 2-person approval flow, ops to prepare audit pipeline with object-lock option and run canary. I'll sync with ACME on allowed egress CIDRs and emergency unwrap policy.
jamie: I'll add a short doc in the private repo: https://redwood.internal/docs/private/acme-egress-kms-playbook (DRAFT).
mike: FYI I'll open a vuln ticket to ensure patched baseline image is baked before canary.
sara: thanks — posting planned changes to PR tomorrow. :thumbsup:
ops: deploy-bot: canary created for ACME dev vpc (canary-id: c-7892). Logs = https://logs.redwood.internal/streams/c-7892
alex: perfect. closing the loop here. if anything urgent ping me directly. :lock:
